frontier.hypothesis: Loop 2's missing copy needs a downstream second use of its base addend, and the only remaining candidate sites are INSIDE loop 2's own if-block, after the do/while - i.e. a statement that target also contains but that we currently spell as a fresh read.
frontier.mechanism: Confirmed this session: the copy survives combine iff its destination has a use reached from the base add (H-s9-1). Loop 1 gets this from `p = q` at its exit tail, whose consumer is loop 2's guard. Loop 2 has no consumer after it because all three of target's remaining ctx+0xC reads (math_Distance3D at T.txt:77, rec_a at :94, rec_b at :104) are emitted as fresh `lw`s and routing any of them through a live local costs 19 points (T1/T3/T4 = 22). The open question is whether some OTHER value - the links pointer, the loop counter, or `base` itself - can carry the liveness instead of the pointer.
frontier.next_probe: On the V1 chassis, sweep second-use carriers for loop 2's base addend that are NOT the ctx+0xC pointer: (a) make loop 2's do/while condition read the count through the addend local rather than through `base`; (b) give the loop-2 links local `lnk2` a post-loop use and derive the base addend from it; (c) assign the addend into the still-live `slots` or `t` local after loop 2 rather than into a fresh dead one (flow.c will not DSE a store to a variable that is read later). Score all of them in one score.sh batch and disassemble anything at 2 or below. Do NOT re-try a source-level `r = p` copy (W1/W2/W3 = 8, killed) or any post-loop-2 use of the pointer in the tail (T family = 22, killed).

frontier.hypothesis: Loop 1's exit tail can emit target's `lw a0,12(s2)` while still supplying loop 1's copy with its second use, if the second use is moved off the tail assignment.
frontier.mechanism: Right now the single statement `p = q;` does double duty: it is q's second use (which buys loop 1's copy, worth 2) and it is the loop-1 exit tail (where target has a fresh re-read, costing 2 because we emit `addu a0,a3,zero` instead of `lw a0,12(s2)`). If some other statement supplied q's second use, the tail could go back to `p = *(u8**)(ctx+0xC);` and the net would be 3 -> 2. The constraint is that the second use must be reached from loop 1's base add and must not itself materialise an instruction target lacks.
frontier.next_probe: On the V1 chassis, try second uses for `q` that are absorbed into instructions target already has: q as the base of loop 1's do/while count reload (`while (i < *(s32 *)(sh + (s32)q + 0x1C))` - target uses `lw v0,28(a0)` off `base`, so this will likely cost an add; measure it), and q as the addend of the loop-1 body's element read. Also measure whether loop 1's copy and loop 2's copy can be bought by the SAME second use by making loop 2's base addend `q` under a pre-initialisation spelling other than X1/X3 (both = 14, killed).

frontier.hypothesis: Every remaining banked spelling conclusion is chassis-relative and must be re-measured before it is spent - the chassis has now changed in EVERY session since s5, and s9 inverted three more s7/s8 kills.
frontier.mechanism: s9 inverted: s7's links-local kill (X1/X2/X3), now worth 2 points; s8's frontier prediction about the shift's four-way assignment, which turned out to be the worst cell in its own space; and s8's 'loop-2 mirror costs 26-31', which was a shared-local artifact and is exactly neutral with per-loop locals. What survives chassis changes untouched is only the pass-level facts, because those are RTL facts rather than score comparisons: H-s6-2, H-s6-3, H-s7-3..H-s7-6, s8's loop.c elimination, and now H-s9-1 (the can_combine_p survival condition) and H-s9-3 (cse+flow kill a source-level copy before combine).
frontier.next_probe: Before spending any banked spelling conclusion, re-run it as a matched pair against V1 with tmp/grind/func_80017848/s9/score.sh. The highest-value untested-on-this-chassis items are the s3-era conclusions about base placement and guard/base role swapping (never retested since s6 retired their chassis) and s8's Z3_swapbase. Note s8's 'per-loop fresh read for the base addend' is now known to be a TIE with `p` (N_P_SF = N_F_SF = 5), not a win, so it is free to change if something else wants it.
